ov: Domesticated ruminants kept for wool, meat and milk, most likely descended from the wild mouflon. There were around 1.2 billion sheep in 2019, and their wool is the most widely used animal fibre.

why.et: Raised for meat, milk, wool and hides in nearly every country; the meat is lamb or mutton.

rg: Farmed across most of the inhabited world, especially in Australia, New Zealand, southern South America, South Africa and the British Isles.
df: Grass and other short plants. Sheep graze close to the ground and avoid the woody growth that goats eat.

cf.tip: A goat usually has a beard and holds its short tail up. A sheep’s tail hangs down, even when short, and its upper lip is split.
